text:
cs-rep: Hi team, customer acme-corp just opened a support ticket — p95 latency for dedicated-usw2 gen2 pool doubled since ~02:00 UTC. They reported timeouts for large chat requests and higher error rate. can we triage?

sara (sre): on it. which models/instances affected? any recent rollouts?

cs-rep: Affected route: /v1/generate (model: seqgen-v2). Only dedicated-usw2; hosted and eu unaffected. No config changes from customer side. Saw spike ~02:10 and persistent.

mike (eng-runtime): thanks. I'll pull perf metrics. preliminary: token p95 went from 180ms -> ~420ms, CPU on worker pods low, but host-level storage wait increased.

jordan (eng-infra): did we push any infra updates last night? kernel/driver/firmware?

nina (ml-infra): We ran a CUDA driver bump on a subset of clusters at 01:30 UTC (12.x -> 13.0.2) as part of staged rollout. Could be correlated.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0423. Pager rota: oncall-sre.

sara (sre): good catch. jordan, can you check NVMe queue depth + iostat on affected hosts? mike, capture a kv-cache hitrate and any tail op logs.

jordan (eng-infra): grabbing logs now. iostat snapshot (abridged):
```
Device:         rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s  rkB/s  wkB/s  avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
nvme0n1        0.00  0.00 10.00 25.00  2048.00 8192.00  320.0    12.50    8.4   1.9    10.5    0.65  60.00
```
avgqu-sz spiked to ~13 on affected hosts. nvme SMART looks healthy.

mike (eng-runtime): kv-cache miss rate up ~15% for seqgen-v2 (we're seeing more cold starts). But storage avg wait incr suggests IO tail causing token latency.

jordan (eng-infra): checked dmesg on one host: repeated NVME timeouts and controller reset traces after driver load:
```
[01:35:12] nvme nvme0: Abort command failed - controller busy
[01:35:13] nvme nvme0: Reset controller due to error
```
Driver version on host: 510.85.12 -> after upgrade to 520.14.08? we have mixed versions across pool.

nina (ml-infra): rollout state: 30% of gen2 hosts moved to 520.x yesterday. Remaining 70% still on 510.x. Could be version skew + firmware sensitivity.

sara (sre): hypothesis: CUDA/driver bump + NVMe driver interaction causing IO retries -> higher storage latency -> p95 spike. Short-term mitigation: divert traffic away from nodes hitting high avgqu, or failover to fallback pool.

mike (eng-runtime): prepared a quick traffic rule to route seqgen-v2 requests from dedicated-usw2 to dedicated-usw2-fallback (older driver hosts) for customers with strict SLOs. Want to flip?

cs-rep: customer requests mitigation asap. please proceed.

jordan (eng-infra): started draining 3 affected nodes and moved their workloads to fallback pool. Also increased per-node NVMe IO scheduler to noop and set /proc/sys/vm/dirty_ratio lower as a temporary measure.

mike (eng-runtime): routing change applied at 03:05 UTC. early metrics: p95 back down to ~220ms for routed traffic, overall pool still noisy as drains continue.

sara (sre): good. we should also roll back the CUDA driver on the small subset that failed if drains don't stabilize. Jordan, open a rollback playbook?

jordan (eng-infra): creating rollback plan now — will target the 30% cohort with controller resets. rollback involves: cordon + drain -> apt remove/replace driver package -> reboot -> sanity checks (nvme stable, iostat avgqu<2). ETA ~90m for phased rollback.

nina (ml-infra): also starting a repro on a repro host: running heavy kv-cache warmup + synthetic generation with long sequences to amplify IO. fio test attached: 
```
fio --name=nvme-tail --filename=/dev/nvme0n1 --rw=randread --bs=4k --iodepth=32 --numjobs=4 --runtime=300
```
we see 99th pct latency > 10ms under the same driver combo where controller resets appear.

mike (eng-runtime): adding a runtime fallback: if storage latency > 5ms, switch to model-quantized variant (seqgen-v2-q8) to reduce KV traffic. Will need a quick config change.

cs-rep: letting customer know we routed their traffic and are rolling back affected nodes. they asked for ETA and asked to avoid data loss.

sara (sre): assigned action items in INC-2026-0423: (1) jordan: rollback cohort or confirm stable driver (2) mike: keep routing and enable runtime fallback (3) nina: finish repro and attach artifacts (4) cs-rep: update customer w/ mitigation + ETA.

jordan (eng-infra): rollback started at 03:45 UTC on node-az3-host12. Reboot completed, nvme avgqu-sz=0.8, no controller logs in dmesg. Marking node healthy.

mike (eng-runtime): post-rollback metrics: routed traffic p95 ~190ms, overall pool p95 trending down to 240ms. quantized fallback config pushed as precaution.

nina (ml-infra): repro artifacts uploaded to internal S3: s3://redwood-debug/inc-2026-0423/fio-results.tar.gz and attached in the incident.

sara (sre): closing immediate mitigation. next steps: schedule full rollback of problematic driver rollout, add preflight NVMe stress test before any future driver rollouts, and add a routing rule to auto-failover on avgqu-sz > 8.

cs-rep: forwarded update to acme-corp — they acknowledged and asked for postmortem.

sara (sre): assigning postmortem to eng-infra + eng-runtime + ml-infra. ops-bot, please add postmortem task to INC-2026-0423 and ping distro tomorrow.

ops-bot: Postmortem task created; reminder scheduled 24h.

mike (eng-runtime): quick note for PMs: consider adding a model-level circuit breaker for storage tail latency so customer-visible SLOs degrade gracefully.

sara (sre): agreed. thanks all for quick response. we will summarize root cause once postmortem completes. :white_check_mark:
